title: Philo of Alexandria, On the Incorruptibility of the World (De aeternitate mundi), section XVI (English, C. D. Yonge, 1855)

source.publisher: Internet Archive (University of Toronto scan of The Works of Philo Judaeus, vol. IV, Bohn 1855)

summary: Philo (about 20 BCE to 50 CE) lists lands and cities the sea has swallowed, as proof that sea level does not show the world is perishing. He cites Plato's Timaeus: the island Atalantes, bigger than Africa and Asia, vanished in one day and night. The only Jewish-Hellenistic account.

tree.title: Philo, On the Incorruptibility of the World XVI (Yonge p. 59; De aeternitate mundi 141): cities lost to the sea, and the island of Atalantes (Plato's Timaeus)
tree.summary: Philo lists Sicily split from Italy and Aegira, Bura and Helice swallowed by the sea. He says the island Atalantes, greater than Africa and Asia, as Plato says in the Timaeus, was overwhelmed in one day and night by earthquake and flood, leaving a sea full of gulfs and eddies.
